prompt: Which 90s virtual pet died if you didn't feed it?
funFact: Over 82 million Tamagotchis have been sold; some schools banned them for causing "funerals".

prompt: Finish the title: The Fresh Prince of ___
funFact: Will Smith took the role partly to pay off a massive tax bill.

prompt: Which toy is a coloured cube you twist to solve?
funFact: Its inventor took a month to solve his own prototype after he had finished building it.

prompt: Which company makes the Mario games?
funFact: Mario wears a cap and moustache because early hardware could not draw hair or a mouth.

prompt: What was a portable CD player commonly called?
funFact: Anti-skip buffers arrived late; before them, walking with one was largely optimistic.

prompt: Which cartoon featured four pizza-loving turtles?
funFact: They began as a black-and-white comic parody, drawn for an adult audience.

prompt: In which board game do you buy property and build hotels?
funFact: An earlier version was designed to teach players that landlords ruin everyone — the lesson did not land.

prompt: What did a dial-up modem famously do while connecting?
funFact: The noise is two modems negotiating a speed; once agreed, they stopped and went quiet.

prompt: Which drink was marketed as "the Uncola"?
funFact: The campaign sold it entirely on not being the thing everyone else was drinking.

prompt: Which home video format outlasted Betamax?
funFact: It won on tape length rather than picture quality — three hours beat one.

prompt: Which falling-block game came bundled with the original Game Boy?
funFact: Bundling Tetris instead of Mario is credited with selling the Game Boy to adults.

prompt: What was Microsoft's animated paperclip assistant called?
funFact: His official name was Clippit. Almost nobody has ever used it.

prompt: Which company made the Walkman?
funFact: Early models had two headphone jacks, because nobody assumed you would want to listen alone.

prompt: Which company made the Mega Drive console?
funFact: Its American advertising attacked a named rival directly, which was almost unheard of at the time.

prompt: Which band released the album "Nevermind"?
funFact: The baby on the cover was paid two hundred dollars, and has since had opinions about it.

prompt: Which band sang "Wonderwall"?
funFact: The title was borrowed from a 1968 film soundtrack by George Harrison.

prompt: Which company made the Game Gear?
funFact: It had a colour screen years before its rival, and ate six batteries in about four hours.

prompt: Which artist released the album "Thriller"?
funFact: Its title video ran fourteen minutes and opened with a disclaimer about the occult.

prompt: Which toy line featured a character called Optimus Prime?
funFact: The toys were two existing Japanese lines, rebranded and given a single story to share.

prompt: Which band recorded "Africa" in 1982?
funFact: None of them had been to the continent; the lyrics were written from television footage.

prompt: In which year did Google launch?
funFact: It started in a rented garage that Google later bought for nostalgia.

prompt: Which group sang "I Want It That Way" (1999)?
funFact: The songwriters barely spoke English — which is why the lyrics famously make no sense.

prompt: In which year did the original Game Boy launch?
funFact: One survived a bombing in the Gulf War, and the scorched unit still switches on.

prompt: In which year did the PlayStation 2 launch?
funFact: It doubled as a DVD player, which for many households was the actual reason to buy one.

prompt: In which year was the first Harry Potter book published?
funFact: The first print run was five hundred copies, and most went straight to libraries.

prompt: Which company created Barbie?
funFact: She was based on a German novelty doll sold to adults, which the company quietly redesigned.

prompt: Which toy caused shop stampedes at Christmas in 1996?
funFact: It cost thirty dollars in shops and was resold for over a thousand at the peak of the panic.

prompt: Which console came with an analogue stick as standard?
funFact: Its rival responded within a year by bolting two sticks onto a controller it had already shipped.

prompt: How many songs did the first iPod promise in your pocket?
funFact: The slogan mattered more than the number — rivals were still quoting megabytes.

prompt: In which decade did the compact disc first go on sale?
funFact: The disc was reportedly sized to hold a whole symphony without turning it over.

prompt: What was the best-selling single of the 1990s worldwide?
funFact: Elton John's Diana tribute sold 33 million copies; he has never performed it again.

prompt: What did the first-ever SMS text message (1992) say?
funFact: Engineer Neil Papworth sent it from a computer — phones couldn't type text yet.

prompt: Nintendo's Virtual Boy was notorious for…
funFact: It was discontinued within a year, and came with a warning about how long children could play.

prompt: What colour was the original Game Boy's screen?
funFact: The olive tint came from the cheap reflective display, not from any design decision.

prompt: What was Pepsi's short-lived clear cola called?
funFact: It tasted like cola but looked like lemonade, and shoppers found that combination unsettling.

prompt: What was the Mega Drive called in North America?
funFact: The name changed because another company already held the European trademark.

prompt: What was the Furby advertised as doing over time?
funFact: It was pre-programmed to shift languages on a timer; it never listened to a word you said.

prompt: The name "SEGA" was shortened from…
funFact: The company began by supplying coin-operated machines to American military bases in Japan.

prompt: What was the Rubik's Cube originally called?
funFact: It was renamed for export, after its Hungarian inventor, when a toy firm licensed it.

prompt: What was the Nintendo Wii called before release?
funFact: The final name was chosen to work in every language, and was mocked in every language.
